problems.title: A sine-and-tangent limit
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to0}(\sin12x-\tan x)/(2x)$.
problems.idea: Use the basic small-angle limits in radians.
formulas: sin u/u→1 and tan u/u→1 as u→0.
steps: Subtract to get 11/2.

problems.title: A derivative that is always positive
problems.question: Solve f′(x)>0 for f(x)=2x³-9x²+24x-36.
problems.idea: Complete the square in the derivative.
steps: Both terms inside the brackets are nonnegative and 7/4 is positive.
Thus f′(x)>0 for every real x.

problems.title: Differentiate a logarithm of a reciprocal
problems.question: Find $f\prime(-2)$ for $f(x)=\ln[1/(x^2+x)]$.
problems.idea: On its domain, rewrite as -ln(x²+x).
steps: The domain is x<-1 or x>0, so -2 is valid.

problems.title: Chain rule through a square root and arcsine
problems.question: Differentiate $y=(\arcsin\sqrt x)^6$.
problems.idea: Differentiate each nested layer.
steps: Combine the factors 6/2 and the square roots.

problems.title: A quotient of small-angle trigonometric terms
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to0}3\tan(2x)/\sin(3x)$.
problems.idea: Extract the angle multipliers.
steps: Write the expression as 2·[tan(2x)/(2x)]/[sin(3x)/(3x)].
Both bracketed ratios tend to 1.

problems.title: Keep the side of an absolute-value limit
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to3^-}(2x^2+4x-30)/|3-x|$.
problems.idea: For x<3, the absolute value is 3-x.
steps: The quotient for x<3 is -2(x+5).
Let x approach 3 from below to obtain -2·8=-16.

problems.title: Rationalize and cancel a common factor
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to1}12(\sqrt{x+8}-3)/(x^3-1)$.
problems.idea: The conjugate creates a factor x-1.
steps: Cancel x-1 for x≠1. The remaining quotient is 12/[(√(x+8)+3)(x²+x+1)].
At x=1 it becomes 12/(6·3)=2/3.

problems.title: A plane through three given points
problems.question: Find the plane through A=(1,2,3),B=(1,1,1),C=(0,0,0).
problems.idea: The origin forces the constant term to vanish.
formulas: A plane through the origin is ux+vy+wz=0.
steps: The points A,B require u+2v+3w=0 and u+v+w=0.
Subtract to get v+2w=0, and then u=w. Choose w=1,v=-2,u=1.
The noncollinear points determine this unique plane.

problems.title: Point-to-plane distance
problems.question: Find the distance from (1,2,3) to 2x+3y-4z-1=0.
problems.idea: Use the absolute plane value divided by normal length.
steps: The numerator is |2+6-12-1|=5.
The normal length is √(4+9+16)=√29.

problems.title: Point-to-line distance
problems.question: Find the distance from (1,2) to 2x+3y-1=0.
problems.idea: Distance is nonnegative.
steps: The numerator is |2+6-1|=7.
The denominator is √13.

problems.title: Rationalize before taking an infinite limit
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to\infty}x(\sqrt{x^2-7x+17}-\sqrt{x^2-7x+7})$.
problems.idea: The root difference has constant numerator 10.
steps: The expression is 10x/(√(x²-7x+17)+√(x²-7x+7)).
Divide by positive x to obtain 10/[√(1-7/x+17/x²)+√(1-7/x+7/x²)].
The denominator tends to 2.

problems.title: Parallel plane normals
problems.question: The planes ax-4y-4z+5=0 and -3x+6y+2bz-10=0 are parallel. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Their normal vectors are proportional.
steps: The y-component gives λ=-3/2.
Then -3=(-3/2)a implies a=2, and 2b=6 implies b=3.
Their sum is 5; the constants are not in the same ratio, so the planes are distinct.

problems.title: Maximum of an exponential quadratic
problems.question: Find the greatest value of y=3^(-2x²+8x-5).
problems.idea: Base 3 increases, so maximize the exponent.
steps: The largest exponent is 3, attained at x=2.
Thus the maximum is 3³=27.

problems.title: Normalize parallel-plane equations
problems.question: Find the distance between 3x+6y+9z+8=0 and 2x+4y+6z+8=0.
problems.idea: First put both equations on the same normal vector.
steps: Divide the equations by 3 and 2 respectively: x+2y+3z+8/3=0 and x+2y+3z+4=0.
The constant difference is 4/3 and the normal length is √14.

problems.title: An angle bisector with duplicated answer choices
problems.question: For A=(-2,0), B=(6,6), C=(1,-4), find the internal angle-bisector line at A.
problems.idea: Add unit vectors along the two sides.
steps: AB=(8,6), length 10; AC=(3,-4), length 5.
The unit-vector sum is (4/5,3/5)+(3/5,-4/5)=(7/5,-1/5), giving slope -1/7.
Through (-2,0), the line is y=-(x+2)/7.
problems.note: The two printed choices y=-0.2x-0.4 and y=-x/5-2/5 duplicate each other, but neither is the bisector. The correct choice is y=-x/7-2/7.

problems.title: Intersect a median and an altitude
problems.question: For A=(2,1),B=(-2,3),C=(0,-3), find the intersection of the median from C and altitude from A.
problems.idea: Write the two lines using a midpoint and perpendicular slopes.
formulas: Midpoint=((x₁+x₂)/2,(y₁+y₂)/2); perpendicular finite slopes multiply to -1.
steps: The midpoint of AB is (0,2), so the median from C is x=0.
BC has slope -3, so the A-altitude has slope 1/3: y-1=(x-2)/3.
At x=0 this gives y=1/3.

problems.title: The correct logarithmic interval is missing
problems.question: Solve $(\ln\pi-1)\log_{1.5}((x-1)/(2x-1))<0$.
problems.idea: The constant factor is positive because π>e.
steps: Require 0<(x-1)/(2x-1)<1. The positive-argument domain is x<1/2 or x>1.
Subtract 1: the upper bound is equivalent to -x/(2x-1)<0, giving x<0 or x>1/2.
Intersect with the domain to get x<0 or x>1.
problems.note: None of the printed choices equals this set. Some choices include points where the logarithm is undefined.

problems.title: Evaluate a trigonometric derivative
problems.question: For f(x)=tanx+cotx+sin2x, find f′(3π/4).
problems.idea: Differentiate term by term, with angles in radians.
steps: At 3π/4 both squared sine and squared cosine are 1/2.
Thus the first two derivative terms cancel: 2-2=0.
The final term is 2cos(3π/2)=0.

problems.title: Stationary points of a rational function
problems.question: Find the smaller root of $f\prime(x)=0$ for $f(x)=(2x^2-3)/(x-3)$.
problems.idea: Apply the quotient rule and solve the numerator equation.
steps: The numerator is 2x²-12x+3. Its roots are (12±√120)/4=(6±√30)/2.
Neither equals 3. Select the smaller root.

problems.title: A line’s angle with the xz-plane
problems.question: Find the sine of the angle between $(x-3)/1=(y+4)/2=(z-17)/(-2)$ and the xz-plane.
problems.idea: The perpendicular-to-plane component is the y-component.
steps: The line direction is (1,2,-2), with length 3.
The xz-plane unit normal is (0,1,0), giving perpendicular component 2.
Hence sinθ=2/3.

problems.title: Compare a rational function with its derivative
problems.question: Solve f′(x)>f(x) for f(x)=(x-1)/(x+1).
problems.idea: The squared denominator is positive on the domain.
steps: Exclude x=-1. Multiply by (x+1)² to get 2>(x-1)(x+1)=x²-1.
Thus x²<3.
Keep the excluded pole out of the resulting interval.

problems.title: Product rule with a tangent
problems.question: Differentiate y=3x³tanx.
problems.idea: Both factors vary with x.
steps: The derivative of 3x³ is 9x².
Hence y′=9x²tanx+3x³/cos²x, wherever cosx≠0.

problems.title: Undo nested logarithms from the outside
problems.question: Solve $\log_2\log_2\log_2x=0$.
problems.idea: Exponentiate one layer at a time.
steps: The outer equation gives log₂log₂x=1.
Then log₂x=2 and x=4.
All nested logarithm arguments are positive at x=4.

problems.title: The coordinates determine the vertex pairing
problems.question: A=(1,-2,3),B=(2,-3,-1),C=(-3,-5,5),D=(a,-6,b) are parallelogram vertices. Find a-b.
problems.idea: Do not assume the listed letters are in cyclic order; test the opposite-vertex sums.
formulas: Opposite parallelogram vertices have the same midpoint, so their vector sums are equal.
steps: If D=A+C-B, its y-coordinate is -4. If D=A+B-C, its y-coordinate is 0. Neither matches -6.
The remaining pairing is A+D=B+C, giving D=B+C-A=(-2,-6,1).
Therefore a=-2,b=1 and a-b=-3.
problems.note: The data require A and D to be opposite vertices. If ABCD were required in cyclic order, the given y-coordinate would be inconsistent; the wording only says the points are vertices.

problems.title: Two parameter signs give the same acute plane angle
problems.question: Find all a for which x+2y+2z+1=0 and 2x-y+3az-1=0 make an acute angle of 60°.
problems.idea: The plane angle uses the absolute dot product of the normals.
steps: The normals are (1,2,2),(2,-1,3a). Their dot product is 6a and lengths are 3,√(5+9a²).
Set |6a|/[3√(5+9a²)]=1/2. Squaring gives 16a²=5+9a².
Thus a²=5/7. Both signs satisfy the original absolute-value equation.
problems.note: Both parameter signs are valid; keeping only the positive sign would discard a correct solution.
